SMTO-EXE-0077 — The computer blocked SMTO from using its clipboard

GUID: 87f99753-3b8e-51e6-b163-50a3e81f66ad
Slug: clipboard-permission-denied
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: clipboard

What happened

  • The operating system on the Gateway computer refused SMTO access to the clipboard, or to a file it was asked to copy. The clipboard was left as it was.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure someone is signed in at the Gateway computer's screen, and that the Gateway (SMTO's helper program there) runs under that same account, not as a background service or another user. The clipboard belongs to the signed-in desktop, so other accounts and background services are refused.
  2. If you asked SMTO to copy a file or picture, check that the Gateway's account can open that file, for example that it isn't in another user's private folder. SMTO opens the file before copying it, and a file it isn't allowed to open causes this refusal.
  3. Ask SMTO to do the clipboard action again. Nothing was changed by the refused attempt, so asking again is safe once access is fixed.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the clipboard action as completed, and pasting on that computer shows the expected content.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't loosen security settings for everything; only give the Gateway the access it needs.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The OS refused the Gateway's clipboard access (Win32 owner window, OpenClipboard or EmptyClipboard failure, or a PermissionError while preparing input files) before any clipboard change.

What this means

  • OS clipboard access or native clear was refused, or file/native preparation raised PermissionError before a possible mutation. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • OS clipboard access or native clear was refused, or file/native preparation raised PermissionError before a possible mutation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect whether session access, source-file permission or a native clipboard action failed; retain its execution certainty.

How to fix it

  • Run the Gateway in the interactive desktop session of the user who owns the clipboard (not session 0, a service account or another user) and verify that account can read any write_files or write_image source paths. Then issue a new explicit request; the refused call did not change the clipboard.
  • Grant clipboard access to the Gateway in the interactive OS session, then make a new explicit request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Grant clipboard access to the Gateway in the interactive OS session, then make a new explicit request.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended explicit operation succeeds under deliberately authorized OS access.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain clipboard write or include content in diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
